genericProblem: A static interaction design can inherit owner assumptions, an action count, or a security negative rule without reopening all same-root sources and later product decisions; the result can be an impossible write path, an unauditable denominator, or a silently contradicted security control.
rootCauseClass: The prior design treated extension rule revision as a universal request fact, action rows as endpoint one-to-one, and an unconditional no-code OTP rule as immutable after Dexter changed the environment-scoped requirement.
finiteDenominator: five extension host types x create/update = 10 request/edge/owner paths
six extension write screens plus six read screens
five OTP display screens and four conflicting frozen rule locations
searchedSurfaces: BusinessEntityService, ContractCommandService, five host create/update callers and Store create request
all operations extension-definition contracts/controllers and all-v2 dynamic-field baseline
app/edge Post/Patch/Put/Delete mappings, IA action screens and P6 action ledger
P6 preparation, IA01, IA05, RM1 plan, current OTP owner/configuration sources
counterexamples: K04 is a retained authenticated administrator recovery chain; X09-X11 remain the old public completion flow.
S04 and S05 are two business surfaces sharing one endpoint, so business-row and endpoint denominators differ.
Production omits a debug field even when DEV/UAT explicitly enable it; omitted is not an empty string.
No enabled definition produces no dynamic field; it does not justify inventing a visible grouping label.

findings.evidence: Store create lacks a revision request fact but its edge caller supplies 0L to a strict owner comparison; other host requests still carry rule revision. Dexter requires every entity extension request revision and owner CAS to be removed while validation and read-only provenance remain.
Three existing operationIds cover all five host types, but twelve IA screens lacked dynamic-field positions; current wires already return extension values.

78 endpoints equal 59 endpoints represented by 56 business rows plus 11 existing exclusions plus 8 unclassified authentication/session endpoints. Dexter retains the 56 business denominator and K04/X09-X11.

Dexter explicitly requires DEV and UAT code display. Existing P-N1 and plan red controls prohibit every response code, so a named amendment and conditional red control are required; v4's session-derived unconditional code is rejected.
